source.section: 21.3 The Adaptive Immune Response: T lymphocytes and Their Functional Types
source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Living in tissues, it takes up and processes antigens and carries them to lymph nodes to activate T cells and start an immune response.
claims.quote: A cell of hematopoietic origin, typically resident in particular tissues, specialized in the uptake, processing, and transport of antigens to lymph nodes for the purpose of stimulating an immune response via T cell activation.

claims.value: It can engulf and kill pathogens by phagocytosis, but its main job is to carry their antigens to the regional draining lymph nodes.
claims.quote: Dendritic cells also kill pathogens by phagocytosis (see ), but their major function is to bring antigens to regional draining lymph nodes.

source.section: 21.3 The Adaptive Immune Response: T lymphocytes and Their Functional Types
source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: In the gut lining it opens the tight junctions between epithelial cells and pushes probes into the lumen to sample microbial antigens, then carries them to nearby lymphoid follicles for T cells to inspect.
claims.quote: Dendritic cells open the tight junctions between epithelial cells and extend probes into the lumen to evaluate the microbial antigens. The dendritic cells with antigens then travel to neighboring lymphoid follicles in the mucosa where T cells inspect for antigens.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: It processes antigen material and sits in the skin (as Langerhans cells) and in the linings of the nose, lungs, stomach and intestines.
claims.quote: Dendritic cells are immune cells that process antigen material; they are present in the skin (Langerhans cells) and the lining of the nose, lungs, stomach, and intestines.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: It is the main antigen-presenting cell of the mucosal immune system; B cells and macrophages play only minor roles there.
claims.quote: APCs of the mucosal immune system are primarily dendritic cells, with B cells and macrophages having minor roles.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

tier1.text: A cell of hematopoietic origin, typically resident in particular tissues, specialized in the uptake, processing, and transport of antigens to lymph nodes for the purpose of stimulating an immune response via T cell activation. These cells are lineage negative (CD3-negative, CD19-negative, CD34-negative, and CD56-negative).
